whatItDoes: Estimates the monthly payment, total cost, and total interest for a fixed-rate auto loan using standard amortization math. You can model different loan amounts, rates, and terms to see the full cost of financing a vehicle.
whyItExists: A car is one of the biggest purchases most people make, yet the monthly payment is often set by a dealer. Knowing the true payment and the total interest help you negotiate a price and term that fit your budget.
whoShouldUse: Car buyers and refinancers comparing loan offers, and anyone checking how a longer term or higher rate changes the total cost before signing.
useCases: Estimate the monthly payment for a target vehicle price
Compare 3-year vs. 5-year loan terms on total cost
See how much interest a longer term adds
Check whether a new car loan fits your monthly budget
Compare a dealer's financing offer against a bank or credit union rate
Decide how big a down payment keeps the payment affordable
instructions: Enter the amount you plan to finance (price minus trade-in and down payment)
Enter the annual interest rate as a percent
Read the monthly payment, total paid, and total interest
Try a shorter term to see the interest saved
Compare a couple of rate scenarios before visiting the dealership
examples: $25,000 at 6.5% for 3 years → payment ≈ $765, but interest drops to ≈ $2,540
bestPractices: Finance only what you need, not the full sticker price
Compare the total-interest column, not just the monthly payment
Add taxes, registration, and dealer fees on top of the payment
Re-run the numbers if your rate or term changes
Get pre-approved by a bank or credit union to negotiate against the dealer's rate
commonMistakes: Financing up to the maximum monthly payment you qualified for
Ignoring taxes and fees in the total cost
Choosing the longest term without checking total interest
Focusing only on the monthly payment while stretching the term to 7+ years
faq: Does this tool support multiple currencies? — Yes, select your currency from the dropdown. All calculations run locally in your browser.
Does this include taxes and fees? — No, it covers the financed amount only.
What is a good auto loan term? — Shorter terms cost less in interest but have higher payments.
Can I include a down payment? — Yes, enter the financed amount after deducting it.
Is my data shared? — No, everything runs locally in your browser.
Should I finance for 5 or 6 years? — Longer terms lower the payment but add interest; pick the shortest term you can comfortably afford.
Is a dealer rate always the best? — Not necessarily; compare against bank and credit union pre-approvals.
assumptions: Standard auto loan amortization; taxes/fees excluded. Generic math applicable globally.
